result.topic_en: This opening page of a continuation of fragments from Euler's mathematical notebooks begins a problem attributed to Lexell: find numbers p, q, r, s that make a given rational expression a perfect square, using successive substitutions.
result.transcription:
Fragmenta ex Adversariis depromta. 487

XXIII.

Continuatio Fragmentorum ex Adversariis mathematicis depromtorum.

(Conf. supra pagg. 157 ad 266.)

I. Supplementa numerorum doctrinae.

91.

(Lexell.)

Problema. Invenire numeros $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$, ut haec formula
$$\frac{\lambda(pp+ss)(qq+rr)}{pqrs(pp-ss)(qq-rr)}$$
fiat quadratum.

Solutio. I. Primo ponatur $pp+ss=(aa+bb)(xx+yy)$ et
$qq+rr=(cc+dd)(xx+yy)$
eritque $p=ax+by$ et $q=cx+dy$
$s=bx-ay$ $r=dx-cy$;
quo facto, quadratum esse debet haec formula:
$$\frac{\lambda(aa+bb)(cc+dd)}{pqrs(p+s)(p-s)(q+r)(q-r)}.$$

II. Ut numerus factorum diminuatur, statuatur $r=s$, sive
$dx-cy=bx-ay$, unde fit $\frac{x}{y}=\frac{a-c}{b-d}$;
fiat ergo $x=a-c$ et $y=b-d$,
unde colligitur $p=aa-ac+bb-bd$, $q=ac-cc+bd-dd$ et
$s=r=ab-bc-ab+ad=ad-bc$, hincque
$p+s=aa-ac+ad+bb-bc-bd$, $q+r=ac-bc-cc+bd+ad-dd$
$p-s=aa-ac-ad+bb+bc-bd$, $q-r=ac+bc-cc+bd-ad-dd$.
Formula ergo quadratum reddenda erit
$$\frac{\lambda(aa+bb)(cc+dd)}{pq(p+s)(p-s)(q+r)(q-r)}.$$

III. Fiat porro $p=cc+dd$, sive $cc+dd=aa-ac+bb-bd$, ad quam resolvendam statuatur $d=a$, eritque $cc=-ac+bb-ba$, sive $0=-cc-ac+bb-ab$, seu $cc+ac-bb+ab=0$, quae per $c+b$ divisa dat $a+c-b=0$, unde fit $c=b-a$ existente $d=a$. Habebimus ergo
$p=cc+dd$, $q=(3a-b)(b-a)$, $r=s=aa+ab-bb$,
unde fit $p+s=a(3a-b)$, $p-s=(b-a)(2b-a)$, $q+r=(2a-b)(2b-a)$, $q-r=a(3b-4a)$.
Consequenter formula quadratum reddenda erit
$$\frac{\lambda(aa+bb)}{(3a-b)(b-a)a(3a-b)(b-a)(2b-a)(2a-b)(2b-a)a(3b-4a)},$$

1*

items.quote:
Invenire numeros $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$, ut haec formula
$$\frac{\lambda(pp+ss)(qq+rr)}{pqrs(pp-ss)(qq-rr)}$$
fiat quadratum.
items.english: Find numbers p, q, r, s such that the formula λ(p²+s²)(q²+r²) / [pqrs(p²−s²)(q²−r²)] becomes a square.
